title: SLO-aware config sweep: per-slice batching & KV-cache drift detection and alerting
creator: Asha Menon
description: Goal: extend the existing config sweep/eval harness to run SLO-aware, per-traffic-slice tests for batching and KV-cache changes and wire automated drift alerts into the Console. The ticket covers: 1) defining traffic slices for monitoring (short prompts, long prompts, few-shot, code-gen, high-QPS clients), 2) running controlled config sweeps that vary batch_size, microbatch shape, kv_cache_ttl, and prefix_cache_enabled flags, 3) computing paired latency and quality distributions per-slice and detecting regressions relative to baseline using robust statistical tests (KS + Bayesian change-point), 4) producing actionable alert rules (severity, required rollback conditions), and 5) integrating the results into the Console SLO dashboards and Alerting pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: 1) New sweep harness can execute N=10 randomized config perturbations across 5 traffic slices and persist per-slice latency & quality time-series to the eval store. 2) Regression detector flags >1 statistically significant quality regression in any slice or sustained latency SLO breach (>5 minutes) and emits a structured alert to the Console alerting endpoint. 3) Alerts include config diff, sample failing prompts, and a recommended fallback config. 4) Runbook for on-call with rollback steps and decorrelated validation checks added to docs. 5) End-to-end smoke test demonstrating detection on synthetic injected regressions.
approach:
- Extend batch-cache sweep harness to accept 'slices' and sample traffic by slice weight.
- For each candidate config, collect per-request metrics: request_type, prompt_length, tokens_out, latency P50/P95/P99, model_version, kv_hit_rate, and quality signals (BLEU/ROUGE-L for structured outputs, token-level logprob drift, and task-specific pass@k when applicable).
- Compute baseline distributions using a rolling 7-day window. Use Kolmogorov-Smirnov to detect distribution shifts and a lightweight Bayesian online change point detector for sustained shifts.
- Use hierarchical decision rule: require (a) quality degradation signal OR (b) latency SLO violation coupled with reduced kv_hit_rate to trigger Medium alert; require cross-slice corroboration or sustained window to trigger High alert + automated circuit breaker.
- Export alerts to Console with a link to a precomputed repro bundle (10 representative requests, diff of config, and small evaluation notebook).
alerting_rules: medium: single-slice quality KS p<0.01 OR latency SLO breach >5min -> page on-call, non-automatic rollback recommended
high: sustained (>30min) quality regression across >=2 slices OR sudden drop in kv_hit_rate with latency SLO breach -> automatic canary circuit-breaker and temporary rollback to pinned config
rollout_plan: 1) Run sweep in sandbox with production-weighted sample traffic (week 0). 2) Run canary in runtime-1.22 env for low-traffic tenant group with strict observability (week 1). 3) If no alerts, scale to 20% of traffic and monitor for 48h. 4) Full rollout if no high-priority alerts after 7 days. Backout path: revert runtime config via release pinning and trigger immediate warm cache refill.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: false positives from natural traffic shifts or eval dataset mismatch. Mitigation: require sustained signal + multiple statistical tests, include 'validation holds' where a secondary evaluation harness replays representative prompts to verify regression. Risk: expensive evals at scale. Mitigation: stratified sampling with importance weights and adaptive sample sizes per-slice.
